decisions.reason: Although its rollout was still incomplete in 2018, the product fits the firm's core dosimetry capabilities and particle-therapy niche, so under bounded rationality management would likely give it more time rather than abandon it quickly.

A small-volume ionization chamber is closely aligned with the firm's established measurement business, and with no visible sign of clear failure the firm would likely retain it while learning from early market feedback.

Even if it overlaps somewhat with other chamber offerings, it remains within the firm's competence base and organizational slack likely supports keeping it on the market until comparative performance becomes clearer.
A standard clinical ionization chamber line with several models sits at the center of the firm's core offering, making it unlikely to fall below aspiration levels so quickly after launch.
This relative-dosimetry chamber serves a specialist but relevant use case for the firm's customer base, so management would probably continue offering it unless clear underperformance emerges.

A thimble ionization chamber is a conventional, complementary product in radiotherapy QA, and a German specialist firm with strong service capabilities would usually keep such a new core-adjacent product in the portfolio.
